questions.stem: A company has a short-term, unpredictable workload that cannot be interrupted. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option fits best?

options.rationale: Spot Instances can be interrupted when AWS needs the capacity back.
On-Demand has no commitment and is not interrupted, which suits short, unpredictable workloads.
Reserved Instances need a one- or three-year commitment.
Dedicated Hosts are for licensing or compliance needs, not short-term flexibility.

questions.explanation: On-Demand: pay by the second or hour with no commitment.

questions.stem: A company runs fault-tolerant batch jobs that can stop and restart at any time. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option offers the largest discount for this workload?

options.rationale: On-Demand is the full price with no discount.
Reserved Instances discount steady usage in exchange for a commitment.
Spot Instances use spare capacity at up to 90 percent off On-Demand, but can be interrupted.
Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware at a higher price.

questions.explanation: Spot is the cheapest option for flexible, interruption-tolerant workloads.

questions.stem: A company has a steady database workload that will run around the clock for the next three years. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option reduces cost the most for it?

options.rationale: On-Demand has no discount for long-term steady use.
A database that must stay up should not run on interruptible capacity.
Dedicated Hosts add cost for single-tenant hardware.
A three-year Reserved Instance commitment gives a large discount for steady usage.

questions.explanation: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans reward predictable, long-running usage with lower prices.

questions.stem: A company wants lower compute prices in exchange for committing to a consistent amount of usage, measured in dollars per hour, that applies across EC2 instance families, AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda. Which option is this?

options.rationale: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2 usage regardless of family, Region or OS, and to Fargate and Lambda.
Standard Reserved Instances apply to EC2 instances, not to Fargate or Lambda.
Spot is not a commitment-based option.
Dedicated Hosts are physical servers, not a usage commitment.

questions.explanation: Savings Plans are a flexible pricing model based on a one- or three-year spend commitment.

questions.stem: A company must use existing server-bound software licenses that are tied to physical sockets and cores. Which Amazon EC2 option supports this?

options.rationale: Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware but do not give socket and core visibility or host control.
Dedicated Hosts give visibility into sockets and cores, which supports server-bound licenses.
Spot Instances are spare capacity at a discount.
Shared tenancy does not give a dedicated physical server.

questions.explanation: Dedicated Hosts are physical servers dedicated to you; they help with licensing and compliance.

questions.stem: A company needs to guarantee EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for a planned event, without a one- or three-year commitment. Which option should it use?

options.rationale: Spot capacity can be reclaimed.
Savings Plans lower prices but do not reserve capacity.
Capacity Reservations reserve capacity in an AZ for any duration, billed at On-Demand rates.
Dedicated Instances are about single-tenant hardware, not reserving capacity.

questions.explanation: Capacity Reservations ensure you can launch instances when you need them.

questions.stem: Several accounts in an organization use consolidated billing. How can a Reserved Instance bought in one account benefit the others?

options.text: It is canceled when the account joins an organization
options.rationale: Joining an organization does not cancel reservations.

options.text: It converts into Spot Instances for the other accounts
options.rationale: Reservations do not become Spot Instances.

options.text: Its discount applies to the purchasing account and nowhere else
options.rationale: Discount sharing is on by default, though it can be turned off.

options.text: Its discount can apply to matching usage in other accounts in the organization
options.rationale: With consolidated billing, RI and Savings Plans discounts are shared across accounts by default.

questions.explanation: The management account can turn off discount sharing for specific accounts if needed.

questions.stem: Which type of data transfer is generally free on AWS?

options.text: Data transferred into AWS from the internet
options.rationale: Inbound data transfer from the internet is generally not charged.

options.text: Data transferred out of AWS to the internet
options.rationale: Outbound transfer to the internet is charged.

options.text: Data transferred between two AWS Regions
options.rationale: Inter-Region transfer is charged.
Transfer between AZs in a Region is generally charged.

questions.explanation: Inbound is generally free; outbound to the internet and across Regions is charged.

questions.stem: Which data transfer typically incurs a charge?

options.text: Data uploaded from the internet into Amazon S3
options.rationale: Inbound transfer from the internet is generally free.

options.text: Data sent from Amazon EC2 in one Region to another Region
options.rationale: Inter-Region data transfer is billed.

options.text: Data moved between Amazon EC2 and Amazon S3 in the same Region
options.rationale: Transfer between EC2 and S3 in the same Region is free.

options.text: Data moved between instances in one Availability Zone over private IP addresses
options.rationale: Same-AZ transfer over private IP addresses is free.

questions.explanation: Keeping traffic in the same Region and AZ, and avoiding unnecessary outbound transfer, lowers costs.

questions.stem: Which TWO factors affect the cost of storing data in Amazon S3? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: The time zone of the AWS Region
options.rationale: Time zones do not affect pricing.

options.text: The number and type of requests made
options.rationale: S3 charges for requests such as PUT and GET, and for retrievals in some classes.

options.text: The number of Availability Zones in the Region
options.rationale: AZ count is not an S3 pricing factor.

options.text: The amount of data stored and its storage class
options.rationale: S3 storage is priced per GB-month, and the price depends on the storage class.

options.text: The number of IAM users in the account
options.rationale: IAM users do not affect S3 pricing.

questions.explanation: S3 costs come from storage, requests and retrievals, data transfer out, and management features.

questions.stem: Which type of Reserved Instance can be exchanged for one with a different instance family during its term?

options.rationale: Standard RIs offer a larger discount but cannot change instance family through exchange.
Convertible RIs can be exchanged for other Convertible RIs with different attributes.
Spot Instances are not reservations.
Dedicated Hosts are physical servers, not a Reserved Instance type.

questions.explanation: Standard RIs trade flexibility for a bigger discount; Convertible RIs trade some discount for flexibility.

questions.stem: Which Amazon EC2 option runs instances on hardware dedicated to a single customer, without giving visibility into sockets and cores?

options.rationale: Dedicated Hosts add visibility into sockets and cores.
Spot Instances use spare capacity on shared hardware.
Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware but without host-level visibility or control.
Capacity Reservations reserve capacity; they do not imply dedicated hardware.

questions.explanation: Choose Dedicated Hosts when licensing needs socket or core visibility; Dedicated Instances when only single tenancy is required.
